question.:question/problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
\mathbf{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_{3}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. The set $\{\mathbf{a}_{1}, \mathbf{a}_{2}, \mathbf{a}_{3}\}$ is linearly dependent.

II. $\mathbf{a}_{1}+\mathbf{a}_{2}-\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$.

III. $2\mathbf{a}_{1}+6\mathbf{a}_{2}-\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A set is **linearly independent** when the equation $x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}+x_{3}\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$ has only the solution $x_{1}=x_{2}=x_{3}=0$. A nontrivial solution proves **linear dependence**.

Test the proposed combination:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{a}_{1}+\mathbf{a}_{2}-\mathbf{a}_{3}&=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}=\mathbf{0}\end{aligned}
$$

Test the proposed combination:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\mathbf{a}_{1}+6\mathbf{a}_{2}-\mathbf{a}_{3}&=2\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+6\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ -6\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{bmatrix}\ne\mathbf{0}\end{aligned}
$$

The homogeneous vector equation gives the coordinate system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1}+x_{3} &=0 \\ 0 &=0 \\ 2x_{1}-x_{2}+x_{3} &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Choose one coefficient nonzero and solve the remaining coordinate equations by substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x_{3}&=1 \\ x_{1}+(1)&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{1}=-1 \\ 2(-1)-x_{2}+(1)&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{2}=-1\end{aligned}
$$

This gives a nontrivial solution. Verify it directly:

$$
-\mathbf{a}_{1}-\mathbf{a}_{2}+\mathbf{a}_{3}=-\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}=\mathbf{0}
$$

The coefficients are not all zero, so the set is **linearly dependent**.

A failed candidate alone does not prove independence; the homogeneous-equation argument settles the classification.

Statement I is **true**. Statement II is **true**. Statement III is **false**.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
\mathbf{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_{3}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. The set $\{\mathbf{a}_{1}, \mathbf{a}_{2}, \mathbf{a}_{3}\}$ is linearly dependent.

II. $-\mathbf{a}_{1}+\mathbf{a}_{2}+3\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$.

III. $-\mathbf{a}_{1}+\mathbf{a}_{2}-3\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A set is **linearly independent** when the equation $x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}+x_{3}\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$ has only the solution $x_{1}=x_{2}=x_{3}=0$. A nontrivial solution proves **linear dependence**.

Test the proposed combination:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\mathbf{a}_{1}+\mathbf{a}_{2}+3\mathbf{a}_{3}&=-\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+3\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\ne\mathbf{0}\end{aligned}
$$

Test the proposed combination:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\mathbf{a}_{1}+\mathbf{a}_{2}-3\mathbf{a}_{3}&=-\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}-3\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\ne\mathbf{0}\end{aligned}
$$

The homogeneous vector equation gives the coordinate system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-x_{1}-x_{2}+x_{3} &=0 \\ -x_{1}+x_{2} &=0 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Choose one coefficient nonzero and solve the remaining coordinate equations by substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x_{1}&=1 \\ -(1)+x_{2}&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{2}=1 \\ -(1)-(1)+x_{3}&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{3}=2\end{aligned}
$$

This gives a nontrivial solution. Verify it directly:

$$
\mathbf{a}_{1}+\mathbf{a}_{2}+2\mathbf{a}_{3}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+2\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}=\mathbf{0}
$$

The coefficients are not all zero, so the set is **linearly dependent**.

A failed candidate alone does not prove independence; the homogeneous-equation argument settles the classification.

Statement I is **true**. Statement II is **false**. Statement III is **false**.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
\mathbf{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_{3}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

I. $-\mathbf{a}_{1}+2\mathbf{a}_{2}-\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$.

II. $-4\mathbf{a}_{1}-2\mathbf{a}_{2}-\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$.

III. The set $\{\mathbf{a}_{1}, \mathbf{a}_{2}, \mathbf{a}_{3}\}$ is linearly independent.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A set is **linearly independent** when the equation $x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}+x_{3}\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$ has only the solution $x_{1}=x_{2}=x_{3}=0$. A nontrivial solution proves **linear dependence**.

Test the proposed combination:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\mathbf{a}_{1}+2\mathbf{a}_{2}-\mathbf{a}_{3}&=-\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+2\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}\ne\mathbf{0}\end{aligned}
$$

Test the proposed combination:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4\mathbf{a}_{1}-2\mathbf{a}_{2}-\mathbf{a}_{3}&=-4\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}-2\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ -4\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}=\mathbf{0}\end{aligned}
$$

The homogeneous vector equation gives the coordinate system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}0 &=0 \\ -x_{2}+2x_{3} &=0 \\ x_{1}-x_{2}-2x_{3} &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Choose one coefficient nonzero and solve the remaining coordinate equations by substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x_{3}&=1 \\ -x_{2}+2(1)&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{2}=2 \\ x_{1}-(2)-2(1)&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{1}=4\end{aligned}
$$

This gives a nontrivial solution. Verify it directly:

$$
4\mathbf{a}_{1}+2\mathbf{a}_{2}+\mathbf{a}_{3}=4\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+2\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}=\mathbf{0}
$$

The coefficients are not all zero, so the set is **linearly dependent**.

A failed candidate alone does not prove independence; the homogeneous-equation argument settles the classification.

Statement I is **false**. Statement II is **true**. Statement III is **false**.
